pages.text: A drunkard's walk of N steps of length l ends about $(thing)l√N$() from where it began - the reason Brownian grains wander as they do. A $(item)Markov Chain Link$() remembers only the one before it; a $(item)Poisson Clock$() ticks at random, each tick a decay in its radium. Clay stirred into water makes a $(fluid)Brownian Suspension$().
The $(item)Confidence Interval Gauge$() shows a range and how sure it is: carried in the off hand, it cancels Variance.
